thread:
maria: Heads-up — hosted API p95/p99 spike started ~4523456700, p95 jumped 180ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~2.8s. Error rate stable, but queue depth and ratecap evictions spiking. Investigating now.
jing: grabbing tracing + kernel selector logs, any deploys around then?
ops-bot: deploy event: service/runtime kselector v2.14 -> v2.15 at 4523456600 by CI (canary 10%).
alex: I see a correlated surge from tenant:analytics-proxy — lots of short-seq requests (~8 tokens) and high fanout. Could be batching/coalescer mispredictions.
maria: attaching tail of runtime logs (snippet):
```
[4523456679] kselector: chosen=aux-kernel (latency_hint=shortseq) seq_len=6 batch_size=32
[4523456682] batcher: coalesced=192 requests latency_wait=15ms queue_depth=48
[4523456683] kvcache: miss_rate=0.62 evictions=120/min
[4523456685] ratecap: tenant_evicts=94 token_burst_rejects=73
```
jing: interesting — kselector flipped to aux-kernel for many shortseqs. Aux kernel has worse tail for high batch_size in current implementation (known tradeoff).
samir: gpu profiler (aggregated 30s window around spike): utilization 84% -> 97%, sm_util spiky, memcpy stalls up 3x.
lisa: add that queue_depth trending looked like a sawtooth — bursts then recovery, not steady. Points to transient noisy tenant rather than global regression.
alex: kvcache miss_rate high too, means more decoding work per request, possible priming churn from the same tenant. Combining shortseq + kv thrash = many small batches with high overhead.
maria: timeline: deploy at 4523456600, spike starts 4523456700, peak 4523456750, partial recovery 4523456900. Matches canary rollout window.
jing: can we correlate which machines saw kernel switch? Querying /internal/kselector/allocs: most switches on pool-hosts in us-east-1-gpu-a.
alex: I pulled trace for one slow request: queue wait 420ms, batch formation 210ms, kernel dispatch 60ms, kv lookup 130ms. p95 dominated by queue wait.
samir: looks like ratecap algorithm started evicting small requests when queue depth exceeded threshold -> head-of-line effect. Short requests get starved by noisy tenant making many tiny requests that saturate batching windows.
lisa: reaction: mute noisy tenant traffic at edge (rate-limit or weight down) and rollback kselector change on canary.
maria: agreed. Can we do a quick canary rollback? Samir you ok to trigger?
samir: initiating rollback to v2.14 on canary group now. ops-bot: rollback started by samir at 4523456950.
ops-bot: rollback complete for canary at 4523457020, rollout hold enforced.
jing: after rollback, p95 back to ~200ms within 3m. p99 back under 400ms. Queue depth normalized.
alex: short-term mitigation: 1) tighten per-tenant burst cap (throttle analytics-proxy to 50 QPS) 2) add a KV prewarm probe for high-fanout tenants 3) add a qdepth-based admission control to avoid H-O-L.
maria: opened runtime backlog ticket: RUNTIME-7159 (triage + followups). Notes: investigate kselector heuristic for shortseq+large-batch interaction, kvcache eviction policy under bursty tenants, add per-tenant sampling for early detection.
jing: also adding a small profiler patch to log kernel choice + batch_size histograms to help future hunts (low-overhead, sampling-based).
lisa: we'll schedule a postmortem doc with charts. For now, ops has throttled analytics-proxy (50qps) and canary rollback held.
samir: follow-up owners: kselector (jing), kvcache (alex), batching (maria). Will sync tomorrow 10am PT.
maria: thanks all — closing active triage. please add any missing observations to RUNTIME-7159. :thumbsup:
